type.description: The message name — <name> in the routing key.

domain.description: The owning domain — <domain> in the routing key. Owned by the Windows State Manager; MTWindows is a Client publishing events in a domain it does not own.

kind.description: Which exchange carries this message. Never reaches the routing key.

ts.description: When the sender published this message, ISO-8601 UTC.

target.description: The WindowId reporting — the <target> routing segment. Required: a window speaks only for itself.

x.description: Left edge, in the reference rectangle's coordinate space.

y.description: Top edge, in the reference rectangle's coordinate space.

width.description: Outer width — chrome included, so a decorations toggle preserves it.

height.description: Outer height — chrome included, so a decorations toggle preserves it.

bounds.description: The window's resolved outer rectangle, as applied — outer, so chrome is included and a decorations toggle preserves it. Same unit and virtual-desktop coordinate space the display source reports its display bounds in; which unit that is per OS is the MTWindows spec's units table, not this field's to restate.

x.description: Left edge of the rectangle the geometry was measured against.

y.description: Top edge of the rectangle the geometry was measured against.

width.description: Width of the rectangle the geometry was measured against.

height.description: Height of the rectangle the geometry was measured against.

reference.description: The rectangle the window overflowed: the resolved display's full bounds or working area for a display-anchored window, the virtual desktop for an OS-explicit one, and the followed window's outer or client area for a following one. One rule, one event, whichever arm the window's position took. Same unit and coordinate space as bounds, so the overhang is bounds minus this.

WindowBoundsOverflowed.description: A window's resolved bounds are not fully inside the rectangle they were measured against. Overflow is allowed, never clamped and never rejected — the bounds stand as computed — but silent on screen is never silent everywhere, so it is reported here.
